title: Set Up Factory AI Automation in 2026 and Know Its Limits
summary: Factory AI automation uses agents to automate coding tasks in your repository.
body_markdown:
## Triggering Factory from outside the repository with Activepieces


Add Activepieces, which connects to 750 integrations, only when the thing that should start a Factory task isn't in your repository, so external integrations become your trigger source.


Even then it changes how a task begins, not what Factory is allowed to do.


Whether a ticket or alert deserves a Factory run is often a judgment a fixed rule can't make, and Activepieces handles that by putting an Agent step in the same flow as the deterministic steps that catch the event and call` droid exec` .


You get one flow definition and one run trace from trigger to result, where an agent framework bolted to a workflow tool by a webhook would leave you reading two logs. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### When Factory's native triggers are enough


Check Factory's own integrations and settings before building anything.


If the task begins with a pull request, an issue or a comment in a tool Factory already connects to, the native path keeps the run inside one product, one set of permissions and one place to read the logs.


Put a second system between the event and the agent and you get a second place for a run to fail silently.


It also keeps your supervised first task honest. You're still learning how Factory behaves on one repeatable job. Adding a workflow engine at that stage mixes two sets of failure modes, and you won't know which one produced a bad result.


### When an external workflow helps


Use Activepieces when the trigger is a ticket in a tracker, a monitoring alert or a submitted form, and no native integration covers it. A workflow catches the event, then an HTTP step calls` droid exec` , Factory's headless mode, or a runner executes it.


On the Free plan, which allows unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, though AI steps cost more.


The result goes back out as a Slack message and a comment on the original ticket.


Follow the illustration below left to right: it traces that path, with a bracket around Factory showing that its limits sit unchanged inside the workflow.


Read it for what the bracket excludes: Activepieces moves the event in and the result out, logging both in a single run trace, and nothing in the middle gets looser.


Practically, that means plan limits, autonomy settings and error behaviour still apply exactly as documented. **A failed run is still a failed run** .


If the HTTP step times out or Factory returns an error, Activepieces will report what it received, so build the Slack and ticket step to post failures as plainly as successes.


Its own credit limit behaves differently: on the Free plan's 1,000 monthly credits, flows stay on and runs wait until credits refresh, which means your automation can experience mid-month execution pauses.


An alert that fires fifty times will start fifty runs unless you throttle it, and your Factory plan, not the workflow, absorbs that load.
